one_pager.big_idea: A verdict is only as good as the data behind it, so scientists follow their plan, record raw data straight away, repeat, and note every anomaly and change honestly.
goals: I can carry out our approved plan safely and record raw data with units, repeats and notes.
I can check the quality of our data, spot anomalies and explain how we handled them.

flow.what: Trays are on the tables before students arrive; hand back the approved plans. Kit check in roles: Safety Officer ticks the tray against the plan's kit list, Lead Scientist reads the method aloud, Recorder copies the results-table headings onto the data sheet, Measurer tests the tools. 'Anything missing? Tell me now.' Slides 1 to 2.
Two data sheets for the same test, one careful and one messy: 'Which would a scientist trust? Why?' Pair talk, then one reason with a frame. Slide 3.

Three data-quality rules (2 min); anomalies and resolution (2 min); safety slide read in both languages (1 min); start signal (2 min): teacher pours warm water for claims 1, 3 and 4 in that order, claim 10 opens bottles together, ice claims take ice from the cool box, everyone starts a stopwatch on 'Go'. Slides 4 to 8, run sheet.

Groups carry out their plans in roles and record raw data in pen; teacher runs the clock from the run sheet: volunteer window opens at minute 16 and closes at minute 28; halfway check at minute 23 ('At least two repeats of each condition?'); two-minute warning at minute 30. Circulate: safety first, then consistency and recording; jot one line per student on the run sheet. Stretch on the worksheet while waiting for readings. Slides 9 to 10. If short: 2 repeats minimum; cooling claims read at 0, 5 and 10 minutes.

'Stop' at minute 32. Clean-up with the kit card (3 min); group data-quality checklist while the teacher photographs or collects every data sheet (2 min); exit ticket (2 min); logbook line 'Our first results suggest ___.' (1 min). Never cut clean-up or the checklist. Slides 11 to 12.

one_pager.practical: Each of the 6 groups carries out its own approved claim investigation from the claim bank at the same time (cooling and ice tests, people tests with volunteers, fizzy drink or paper towel tests), recording raw data in pen on a group data sheet with at least 2 repeats of each condition (3 the target).
one_pager.assessment: One data sheet per group (raw data, notes, changes), photographed or collected before students leave: the main evidence for rubric strand 3 (Doing and recording). Teacher's run-sheet notes, one line per student, support individual strand 3 levels. Exit ticket: repeats achieved, one data-quality action, one problem. Logbook line under 'What I found'.
hazards: Ice and salt mixtures are cold enough to hurt skin: gloves on; handle tubes and cups, never the mixture.
Warm water can scald: only the teacher prepares and pours it, no hotter than about 60 °C (about 50 °C for claims 3 and 4); cups and bottles stay on the tray.
No eating or drinking: nothing used in an investigation is eaten or drunk, including ice, salt and fizzy drinks.
Glass thermometers break easily: never stir with one or pull one out of ice; if one breaks, step back and tell the teacher.
Spills make floors slippery: wipe up at once.
Human participants: voluntary, no pressure, codes not names; anyone can stop or withdraw their results.
Tape measures can snap back: retract slowly and keep the metal end away from faces. Ruler drop: sit for every test.
one_pager.language_note: Frames: 'We noticed an anomaly in ___. We think it happened because ___. We ___ (repeated it / kept it and noted it).' 'We changed our plan because ___.' 'The data suggests ___; however, ___.' 'Would you like to take part in a short test? You can say no or stop at any time.' Chinese talk is welcome while working; readings are called out in English numbers ('thirty-four point five degrees'). Traps: 'raw' means not yet calculated, not uncooked; 'resolution' is not a New Year's resolution; 'consistent' is not 'constant'; an anomaly is an unusual result, not a mistake: it is checked, not deleted.
watch_out: 'An anomaly is a mistake, so we rub it out.' Circle it, note it, repeat if possible; never hide it.
'We changed the plan, so our results are ruined.' Sensible changes are fine if written down with a reason (rubric strand 3, Excellent).
'More decimal places means better data.' Write only what the tool can show (its resolution).
'If the result is what we predicted, the data must be good.' Good data is about method, not the answer.

Investigation day fails if kit is hunted for during the lesson: build the trays the day before from the approval stubs. Do not give expected results before data is collected; claim 2 groups will be surprised (ask 'What did the colour do?').

Print data sheet photos for any group whose original is missing or damaged. During this week, for Week 9: print reviewer checklists and self-assessment slips (1 per student). Keep the run-sheet notes for the strand 3 judgement before Week 10.

Kit card copies: the design (Kit-card.dc.html) is marked 'Teacher copy', but the timeline and slide 11 have students 'clean up with the kit card'. Print 6 group copies as well, or project the clean-up list?

Data-quality checklist: slide 11 speaker notes say 'write why in the notes box', but the 6c card (lesson file and Checklist.dc.html) has no notes box, only 'Not yet, because ___'. Should notes go on the data sheet's 'Problems and observations' box?

Thermometers: the kit card says 'about 12 in the class', but the tray labels (6d) allow 3 to 6 for claim 3 and 2 to 6 for claim 4, plus 2 each for claims 1 and 6, 1 for claim 2, teacher spares and one for checking the warm water. Is 12 enough for the claims chosen?

Ice: the kit card says about 1 kg per ice claim group, but Teacher_Guide.md Section 7 lists Year 9 ice only for Week 6 (2 to 3 kg), and the Week 8 file does not say who crushes the 300 g of crushed ice for claim 6, or when the optional food colouring is added to the ice for claim 2. No amount of salt is stated.

Run sheet (6a): the lesson file says 'A4, 1 copy', the design has 2 pages (timeline; group grid) and does not say single or double sided. The grid is written on, so 1 copy per class was entered.
Stopwatches and paper towels: the kit card puts 1 stopwatch on every tray but claim 8's label asks for 2; 'paper towels: 1 each' does not say roll, pack or sheets.

Claim 12 needs two time slots ('Agreed time slots' on the run sheet); the arrangement is left to the teacher (Y9_W07 notes suggest a supervised 5-minute slot, for example after lunch). When, where and who supervises is not recorded in the files.
Storage: the files do not say where the approved plans, data sheet originals and photos are kept between Weeks 7, 8 and 9 (class box or teacher's folder).
Role cards are not named in the Week 8 file although the kit check is run by role; Teacher_Guide.md has role cards on every table. Entered as reused.

Pour away ice, salt, drinks; read exit tickets; keep data sheets for Week 9

print_items: Group data sheet x12, A4 double-sided (2 per group)
Data-quality checklist x6, A5, laminated if possible (1 per group)
Tray labels: 2 A4 sheets, only the chosen claims' labels
Teacher copies: run sheet (2 pages, per class), kit card (A5, 2 sides)
Claim 7: word lists A and B x6 each (A5), recall sheets, marking key
Claim 8: number hunt layout A x6, layout B x2 (A4)
Script card (A6): 1 per people-testing group, plus spares
get_items: Pens, not pencils x24 (4 per group)
Thermometers, about 12, shared out, plus spares
Kettle, flask(s) and jug for warm water (teacher only)
Plan A: cool box, ice (about 1 kg per ice claim group), salt
Gloves, goggles, bucket and cloth, paper towels
Claim kit as on each tray label (scales, cups, bottles, fabric, tape measures)
Phone or camera; clipboard; device and headphones (claim 7)
Make: 6 group trays; freezing mixture (claim 1); towel brands A, B, C
reuse_items: Approved plans and signed approval slips x6 (Week 7)
Week 3 ruler-drop cards and conversion tables (claim 12)
hazards: Ice and salt mixtures: gloves on; handle tubes and cups, never the mixture
Warm water: teacher pours only, no hotter than about 60 °C; cups stay on the tray
Nothing eaten or drunk; never stir with glass thermometers; wipe up spills at once
People tests: voluntary, no pressure, codes not names; retract tape measures slowly
watch_out: 'An anomaly is a mistake': circle it, note it, repeat if possible; never rub it out.
'We changed the plan, so results are ruined': changes are fine if written down with a reason.
Kit hunted for mid-lesson sinks the day: build trays the day before; never cut clean-up or the checklist.
one_pager_text.language_note: Frame: 'The data suggests ___; however, ___.' 'Raw' means not yet calculated; 'consistent' is not 'constant'. Readings in English numbers.
one_pager_text.next_week: Keep data sheets and photos safe: Week 9 reports are written from them; print reviewer checklists
